Senses.Explanation: The “original face” is the face a person is challenged to recognize or investigate before acquired distinctions settle the answer. The records repeatedly preserve Huineng’s question to Ming: when not thinking good and not thinking evil, “what is your original face?” (不思善不思惡，正恁麼時，如何是上座本來面目). Tianyin Yuanxiu quotes that question and the instruction to turn the light back upon one’s own original face. Guanyin Congxian deliberately removes the four words “original face” from Huineng’s demand and asks whether the alteration still belongs to Huineng’s lineage. Dahui Zonggao pairs the phrase with one’s home-ground scenery and says that the original face itself has never been deluded or awakened, locating delusion and awakening in a person’s momentary thought. Yulin Tongxiu tells the emperor to investigate the phrase in activity as well as stillness. Zhuanyu Guanheng equates the six sense-fields, when recollected without discrimination, with one’s own original face. Miyun Yuanwu urges recognition of it amid ordinary bending and looking up, then answers his own renewed question with a shout and a spatial saying. Yushan Shangsi makes his staff leap into a hall, knock down the person of no rank, and smash the original face in a deliberately extravagant hall address. Across these uses the phrase is a question, an object of investigation and recognition, an explicit equation, and a target of corrective wordplay; no single verbal reply is made its universal definition.

Senses.Explanation: Speech proper to the matter is language the records mark as belonging to the essential business of the house, while still testing whether it fits the person and occasion. Dahui Zonggao gives the limit directly: an extravagant staff-and-fan saying may be proper to the matter, yet an unprepared hearer cannot understand it, so Dahui requires the approach to fit the hearer without replacing the matter. Meixi Fudu sets such speech aside and demands a departing word, showing that the label does not finish an interview by itself. Yuanwu Keqin uses it to approve Xuedou's line after rejecting a quiet-mind explanation, while Wansong Xingxiu grants plain proper-to-the-matter discussion and then points to a further living road. The expression is therefore neither a blanket compliment nor a special vocabulary list; it is a public judgment that speech belongs to the matter, tested again by audience, timing, and response.

Senses.Explanation: The saying, question, or public case singled out as a person's main subject of inquiry. The possessives and verbal predicates in later Chinese Chan records make this local use concrete. Jiexian tells a hall leader to know each person's own word or saying under primary investigation; another passage says that not knowing it leaves the leader without a way to act. Zhanran Yuancheng tells people to place the selected saying before their eyes, Konggu Daocheng says to raise it, and Langting Jingting warns Qianyun that he has dropped one line of it behind his head. The compound can take 'public case' or 'word, saying, conversational thread' after it, and can itself be said to be broken through. Yongzheng asks, 'What is primary investigation?' and gives one particular example: if one trusts the gate of recollecting buddha, investigate who is recollecting buddha. Wuyi Yuanlai says that the Chan house relies on primary investigation and that when it breaks through it is like the moon reflected in a thousand rivers. These predicates describe the assigned subject and the act of investigating it without turning the term into a named system.

Senses.Note: The possessive is part of the corpus usage: it is the particular phrase or unresolved point a person is carrying, not a name for every old case indiscriminately.

Senses.Explanation: One's own case-phrase is the particular unresolved point in a saying or case that the student cannot yet get through and keeps immediately at hand. Poshan Haiming defines it from the obstruction itself: whatever remains unclear and unpenetrated in a teaching or public case is precisely the personal case-phrase. Zen bends the 'phrase' into the student's live obstruction: it travels through ordinary activity and is tested by whether the unresolved point actually breaks open.

Senses.Explanation: One's nature as it is from the outset. Chan records repeatedly use 'see one's own original nature' beside 'recognize one's own original mind.' The Platform Record makes seeing it the distinction between remaining outside the gate and entering, and describes it as not arising or extinguishing. The Mirror Record says that original nature has no difference and is not obtained because of conduct. These are the texts' recorded descriptions; the English should preserve the plain noun phrase rather than substitute a later explanatory system. The omitted collocation "original nature empty" (本性空) occurs forty times in thirty texts, but it has more than one syntax. Twenty-seven occurrences in twenty-five texts belong to the fixed line, "understand body and mind, original nature empty; how would this person differ from buddha?" (了得身心本性空，斯人與佛何殊別). A later Chan address raises that line and immediately comments, "the buddha-body is neither real nor empty; buddha-as-appearance is not appearance" (佛身無實亦無虗，佛幻非幻). The Source-Mirror Record gives a separate explicit definition: "as for original-nature empty, it is the own-nature clear-and-clean mind; original nature is own nature; empty means clear and clean" (本性空者，即是自性清淨心；本性即自性；空，即清淨義).

Senses.Explanation: All things are consciousness-only is an inherited proposition that Chan records repeatedly put under pressure in face-to-face questioning. Yongming Yanshou presents it as a scriptural formula, but Huangbo Xiyun says the paired mind-only and consciousness-only wording was spoken against outside wrong views and refuses to make it a final resting place. Xitang Zhizang asks a purple-robed lecturer to state consciousness-only, then points to the door panel and asks what it is. In the Fayan case, Luohan Guichen invokes the same formula before asking whether a courtyard stone is inside or outside mind. Bie'an Xingtong retells Guichen’s test after rejecting the explicitly unnamed questioner’s conceptual explanation as ‘not yet’; Dahui Zonggao likewise describes Xiaonan as having mastered the formula before a separate encounter overturned that settled account. The entry therefore records both the proposition and its observable Chan use as material for testing. It does not adopt an outside systematic exposition as the definition of Zen.

Masters use the place formula as a spoken verdict: a proposed middle, a two-sided escape, a delayed answer, or another proposed position or verbal move is nowhere near. Shexian Guisheng answers the upward matter with the full departing-for-Yazhou couplet. Zhongfeng says trying to suppress motion and stillness is not yet even as near as Yazhou; Guanghui Lian rejects both having and lacking guest and host; Shanhui applies it when neither side nor middle remains; Yuan’an Liao answers one participant with a remade couplet; Yanxi Guangwen applies it to grasping “not mind, not buddha.”

Senses.Explanation: A paste cake is a prepared flour cake that becomes a compact answer and case object. Yunmen Wenyan answers the public request for talk beyond buddhas and ancestors with ‘paste cake’; Jiashan Shanhui holds one up to Luopu while pressing the claim that the many kinds do not leave this one. Later masters quote, verse, and criticize those uses, so the food remains concrete even when it is wielded in an interview.
